title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The document “Decision of the AI Office” outlines the office’s final stance on a specific AI-related issue, detailing the criteria and reasoning behind the decision. It also specifies the next steps and any actions required to implement or enforce the decision.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The policy explains how to create and manage job openings for AI technology specialists. It outlines the qualifications, duties, and hiring procedures for these AI specialist roles.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: This document announces a vacancy for a Lead Scientific Adviser in the AI Office. The role involves overseeing research, guiding policy, and ensuring ethical AI practices.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: This document announces a vacancy for legal officers within the AI Office. It outlines the duties, required qualifications, and application procedure for candidates who will oversee the legal aspects of the organization’s AI projects.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: This policy explains the roles and responsibilities of AI Office Policy Officers, including the criteria for hiring and the responsibilities they hold in guiding AI governance. It also outlines the procedures for filling vacancies and ensuring that officers adhere to ethical guidelines and compliance standards.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts convened to evaluate the impact of the EU's proposed AI regulation. They provide evidence‑based recommendations on safety, transparency, and oversight to guide policymakers in drafting balanced AI legislation.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: The document is a preliminary request to develop standardized guidelines for a particular area. It aims to bring uniformity and consistency to related processes and practices.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This document announces a consultation period for members of the Community of Practice (CoP) to provide feedback on proposed AI policy changes. It invites stakeholders to review and share their input before finalizing the policy.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: The document invites individuals or groups to express interest in creating or joining a Community of Practice focused on AI policy. It encourages collaboration, outlines the purpose and scope of the group, and welcomes expertise sharing among participants.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The document offers a visual guide to a Community of Practice’s iterative drafting process, mapping out how draft content is created, reviewed, and refined across multiple rounds. It illustrates key stages—including initial drafting, feedback collection, revisions, and final approval—to highlight collaboration and continuous improvement.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: This document presents a graphic that illustrates the chronological sequence of steps taken during the drafting of the AI policy. It serves as a visual reference to understand the development timeline and key milestones.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: The "Code of Practice: 1st Draft" outlines basic rules and standards that developers and users should follow when creating and deploying artificial intelligence systems. It emphasizes responsible design, transparency, fairness, and accountability to ensure AI is safe, ethical, and aligned with societal values.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: This document outlines the second draft of a Code of Practice for responsible AI use, detailing principles and guidelines for developers, organizations, and users. It aims to promote transparency, safety, and accountability in AI systems by setting clear standards and expectations.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 3rd Draft is a set of guidelines that outline best practices for the responsible design, development, and deployment of artificial intelligence systems. It covers key areas such as transparency, fairness, accountability, and safety to help organizations implement AI in a way that aligns with ethical standards and regulatory expectations.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft is a proposed agreement outlining principles and commitments for responsible AI development and use. It aims to establish standards, governance frameworks, and collaboration among stakeholders to ensure transparency, fairness, and accountability in AI systems.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final establishes a global agreement aimed at ensuring that artificial intelligence is developed and used responsibly, with a focus on safety, fairness, and human well‑being. It calls for collaborative governance, transparency, and shared standards among governments, industry, and civil society to manage risks and promote the benefits of AI for all.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: The guidelines identify specific AI practices that are disallowed, including those that could manipulate opinions, generate disallowed content, or violate privacy. They set clear rules to ensure AI is used responsibly and ethically, protecting users' rights and safety.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This document provides guidelines for defining what constitutes an AI system, outlining key characteristics and components. It helps organizations classify and manage AI technology by establishing clear criteria for identifying and labeling AI systems.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy focuses on using clear communication strategies to support and accelerate startup growth and innovation. It highlights collaboration, funding, mentorship, and public outreach to build an ecosystem that helps new ventures develop, launch, and thrive.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a program that helps early‑stage companies tap into high‑performance computing resources across Europe. It provides funding, mentorship, and shared infrastructure to accelerate innovation and boost the competitiveness of new tech ventures in the HPC sector.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This slideshow outlines a webinar on risk management, explaining how businesses can identify, evaluate, and address potential threats. It covers practical strategies and best practices for reducing risk and protecting organizational assets.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar explores the essential principles of risk management in AI, explaining how organizations can identify potential risks, assess their impact, and implement mitigation strategies. It also offers practical guidance on developing robust risk‑management policies, monitoring processes, and ensuring compliance with legal and ethical standards.
